newsitem.title: USA: Mercury secures $50 mln in financing.
newsitem.headline: Mercury secures $50 mln in financing.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co said Monday it has secured $50 million in short-term financing from Bank of America.
The financing is secured by Mercury's assets, the Lake Forest, Ill.-based sub-prime auto lender said in a news release.
Funds will be used to meet day-to-day operating expenses and cover interest payments that are coming due in the next few weeks, Mercury said.

It said it continues to work toward completing longer-term financing arrangements to raise funds to cover principal and interest obligations that have matured, and to reestablish a stable financial footing for the business going forward.

Mercury said last week it had been unable to finance $61 million in short-term commercial debt that had matured through February 5 and that another $127 million would come due between then and February 14.
Mercury's woes began January 29 when it said its earnings of the last four years would have to be restated downward by about $90 million due to accounting irregularities.

Since then, the company has defaulted on millions of dollars in debt, een served with a search warrant by federal agents seeking financial records, hired turnaround and bankruptcy specialist William Brandt Jr as chief executive officer, and been named a defendant in more than half a dozen lawsuits surrounding the restated earnings.
Mercury, whose stock was halted on the New York Stock Exchange pending news Monday afternoon, said it continues to serve customers at all of its locations nationwide.
Mercury shares were halted at 2-1/4, up 3/8.
